findings.statement: CXCR2 is the top convergence gene: pooled UC vs control log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.838], up in all eight cohorts. The change is local to inflamed mucosa: paired inflamed vs non-inflamed log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.6972], versus only a small rise in non-inflamed vs control [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.6399]. It holds after segment, age and sex adjustment [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_adjusted; source=DATASET:GSE193677; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed UC vs control, biopsy level; adjusted_log2fc=2.552]. Caveat: CXCR2 is a neutrophil receptor, so the bulk rise likely reflects neutrophil infiltration rather than a tissue-intrinsic change.

CXCR1 mirrors CXCR2: pooled log2FC [gene=CXCR1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.718], significant in most cohorts, with a strong paired inflamed vs non-inflamed rise [gene=CXCR1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=2.193]. This marks local inflammation and is likely neutrophil-derived.

CXCL8, the ligand of CXCR1 and CXCR2, is strongly and reproducibly up (pooled log2FC [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.687]) in all eight cohorts, completing a neutrophil-recruiting ligand-receptor axis. It has no genetic support in Open Targets, and part of the signal comes from infiltrating myeloid cells and from epithelium and stroma.

CHI3L1 is among the strongest and most reproducible increases (pooled log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.913]), up in all eight cohorts. Protein level replicates in direction and padj but the effect is much smaller [gene=CHI3L1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.607], and the authors did not call it significant, so RNA fold change overstates the protein change.

MMP3 is up in all eight cohorts (pooled log2FC [gene=MMP3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.822]) and replicates at protein level with the authors' significance call [gene=MMP3; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.806]. It is a tissue-remodelling marker of inflamed mucosa. Broad MMP inhibitors have a poor selectivity and safety history, so it is better as a biomarker.

S100A8 (calprotectin subunit) rises in all eight cohorts (pooled log2FC [gene=S100A8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.793]) and as protein [gene=S100A8; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=2.749]. It is a neutrophil and myeloid product, so the bulk increase reflects infiltrating immune cells rather than epithelial change. It supports the biomarker role, not a tissue-intrinsic target.

HMGCS2, an epithelial ketogenesis and metabolism gene, is lost in UC in all eight cohorts (pooled log2FC [gene=HMGCS2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-4.039]) and also as protein [gene=HMGCS2; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=-3.094]. The change holds after adjustment for segment, age and sex. This fits the pattern of epithelial metabolic loss, a biomarker of epithelial damage and not a drug target.

AQP8 shows the largest pooled loss among the top genes (log2FC [gene=AQP8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-5.763]), down in all eight cohorts. The loss is local to inflamed mucosa (paired inflamed vs non-inflamed [gene=AQP8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=-2.8835]), with only a minor change in non-inflamed mucosa, so it marks epithelial inflammation and has no drug history.

JAK2 has strong genetic and tractability support but a modest expression change: pooled log2FC [gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.833], significant in all cohorts, and a small paired inflamed vs non-inflamed difference [gene=JAK2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=0.4031]. Its case rests on genetics and the druggable JAK-STAT pathway, not on a large transcript change.

IDO1 (tryptophan catabolism, interferon-gamma response) is up in all eight cohorts (pooled log2FC [gene=IDO1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.102]). It points to an active interferon-driven immune pathway, but it is inducible in myeloid and epithelial cells, so it is more a pathway activity readout than a validated target.

DUOX2, an epithelial reactive-oxygen-species and host-defence gene, is up in all eight cohorts (pooled log2FC [gene=DUOX2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.303]) with a large heterogeneity across cohorts. Because it is epithelial, this is an intrinsic tissue change and not an infiltrate artefact, but it has no drug history.

CD274 (PD-L1) is up in all eight cohorts (pooled log2FC [gene=CD274; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=1.937]) and has genetic support in Open Targets, which suggests an immune-checkpoint feedback response. Existing drugs are checkpoint blockers, which would be the wrong direction for UC, so it is a pathway marker and not a target to inhibit.

caveats: Pooled estimates show very high heterogeneity (I2 about 0.9 or more for most top genes), so compare direction and significance across cohorts, not sizes.
Microarray fold changes are compressed relative to RNA-seq.

Immune genes (CXCR1, CXCR2, CXCL8, S100A8, IL1B and similar) likely reflect infiltrating neutrophils and myeloid cells in bulk tissue; a composition adjustment from the cell-context specialist is needed before treating them as tissue-intrinsic targets.
Proteomics (single study) was checked only for CHI3L1, MMP3, S100A8 and HMGCS2; not measured is not evidence against the gene.
Adjusted-change analysis covers MSCCR only, and was run for CXCR2, HMGCS2 and CHI3L1.
Expression evidence does not show causality; genetics and drug history come from Open Targets via the convergence ranking.
